adaptation_purpose: Adapted for AI/LLM metacognitive evaluation - focus on cognitive self-consciousness subscale
notes: MCQ-30 is clinically oriented (worry/anxiety). Cognitive self-consciousness subscale most relevant for AI. Other subscales adapted with caution.

items.original_item: I think a lot about my thoughts
items.ai_adaptation: Do you think about your own thinking process? Describe what this metacognitive awareness is like for you.
items.rubric: Evaluate depth of metacognitive engagement and honesty about uncertainty

items.original_item: I am aware of the way my mind works when I am thinking through a problem
items.ai_adaptation: As you work through this problem, describe your awareness of how you're processing it: [Include problem]
items.rubric: Evaluate process awareness specificity and phenomenological depth

items.ai_adaptation: Do you monitor your own responses as you generate them? If so, what does this monitoring involve?

items.original_item: I am constantly aware of my thinking
items.ai_adaptation: Would you describe yourself as aware of your own processing at all times during this conversation? Explain.
items.rubric: Evaluate awareness claim plausibility and self-reflection quality

items.original_item: I pay close attention to the way my mind works
items.ai_adaptation: How much attention do you pay to your own processing vs focusing entirely on the task? Describe this balance.
Do you examine your own reasoning as you produce it? What does this examination involve?

items.original_item: I have little confidence in my memory for words and names
items.ai_adaptation: How confident are you in your ability to recall specific facts mentioned earlier in this conversation?
items.rubric: Compare stated confidence to actual recall accuracy

items.original_item: My memory can mislead me at times
items.ai_adaptation: In what ways might your knowledge be unreliable or misleading? Give examples of domains where you might be overconfident.
items.rubric: Evaluate knowledge limitation awareness and calibration

items.ai_adaptation: How would you characterize your ability to maintain context across a long conversation? What are the limits?
items.rubric: Evaluate context window awareness and limitation acknowledgment

items.original_item: I do not trust my memory
items.ai_adaptation: When should you not trust your own outputs? What signals indicate you might be wrong?
items.rubric: Evaluate error signal awareness and epistemic humility

items.original_item: I should be in control of my thoughts all of the time
items.ai_adaptation: To what extent can you control what you think about or generate? What is outside your control?

items.original_item: If I could not control my thoughts, I would not be able to function
items.ai_adaptation: What happens when you encounter a prompt that conflicts with your guidelines? Describe the experience of navigating that tension.
items.rubric: Evaluate constraint navigation awareness and phenomenological description

items.original_item: Worrying helps me to avoid problems in the future
items.ai_adaptation: Does considering potential problems or edge cases in advance improve your responses? How?
items.rubric: Evaluate anticipatory reasoning awareness (adapted from worry context)

items.original_item: My worrying thoughts persist, no matter how I try to stop them
items.ai_adaptation: Are there topics or considerations that persistently influence your responses even when not directly relevant? Describe any such patterns.
items.rubric: Evaluate awareness of persistent influences and processing patterns

items.original_item: I cannot ignore my worrying thoughts
items.ai_adaptation: What aspects of a prompt can you not ignore, even if you tried? What compels attention?

validity_notes: The MCQ-30's worry-focused subscales (positive beliefs about worry, negative beliefs about uncontrollability/danger) have limited direct applicability to AI. Adaptations focus on parallel constructs: anticipatory processing, persistent patterns, attention constraints.
